actual_scope: F2[S4] register word with three binary scalar roles; only paid address letters are adjacent transpositions s1=(12), s2=(23), s3=(34), at one call each; rank-one idempotent scalar mixers N=uv^T over F2 with v^Tu=1; target diag([c],[c],[e]) for c=s1*s2*s3 (a 4-cycle), with arbitrary dirty inputs; test whether any exact word uses at most five calls, versus the direct six-call word.
scope_change_reason: The suggested nonabelian/new-register track is refined to a new address group and paid alphabet: adjacent transpositions in S4, three scalar roles, and two repeated 4-cycle targets. Recent live work already covers the same UT3 commutator target at r=2,3 (PR1478), coordinate-SWAP targets over GL2 at r=4 (PR1705), two affine targets over AGL2 (PR1711), and four-register rational frame relations (Discussion1700). The S4 target and alphabet do not duplicate those scopes.
bottleneck_link: This attempt tests whether a new bit-register address alphabet offers a local cost reduction; the current selected binding-only screen reports the complex primitive as binding. The proposed S4 saving did not occur: exact minimum is six, so this mechanism yields no paid-call reduction or recursive-moment change.
stop_rule: Completed: exact radius-2/radius-3 meet enumerated all words through length five. No word is found; six-call direct word verified. Search would stop and report incomplete if the 110-second code cap or 1-GiB RSS cap were reached. No widening to other targets or groups.
evidence: Exact F2[S4] search over all 84 paid involutions. Identity-side layers [1,84,4697] (4782 states); target-side layers [1,84,4697,232692] (237474 states); intersection empty. Literal convolution checks all 84 generators square to identity, verifies the six-call direct word, rejects six single-call omissions and rejects the changed-third-role endpoint. Reproduced in 2.29 seconds at 60576 KiB RSS on Python 3.12.3; certificate is CERTIFICATE.json. This is a scoped exact minimum six in the declared model, not a physical supplier or kappa result.
